recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-37822; any future broader HTTP header table cleanup should be handled under a separate tracker.
issue_request: FHIR-37822 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for R5. It requested that Prefer: handling=strict and Prefer: handling=lenient be officially defined on the HTTP page while the search page retained the explanation of how those preferences are used and linked to the official definition.
initial_application: The request was applied by commit 7415a1eb0824ba59d977db335205d71eed004312, which added the HTTP Headers section to source/http.html and changed source/search.html to link the search handling-strict/lenient prose to http.html#Http-Headers. The same historical commit also applied the separate FHIR-35859 POST-search clarification.
additional_context: source/hierarchy.xml places source/http.html in the built RESTful API page and source/search.html as its Search child page. FHIR-I minutes from 2022-08-01 confirm the Persuasive with Modification vote at 14-0-0, and a 2022-09-01 Zulip implementation thread clarifies that FHIR-37822 was about search-related headers rather than unrelated HTTP header cleanup.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source/http.html HTTP Headers table includes a Prefer request-header row citing RFC 7240 processing preference and linking to Search: Handling Errors, while source/search.html still describes handling=strict and handling=lenient and links to http.html#Http-Headers. The combined branch had no prior FHIR-37822 reconciliation commit and already contained the correct source state.

related_jiras.note: The historical implementation commit also applied POST-based search clarifications in source/http.html and source/search.html, but that request is separable from the search Prefer header placement audited for FHIR-37822.
